correctness.rationale: PROVED part verified by independent re-derivation and re-execution. (1) |R-Q/2|=|S|/2 is exact. Lemma 2 orthogonality with zero-extension is correct, checked case-by-case. Lemma 3 conductor q=pf dividing pm and chi*psi nonprincipal is correct; coprime-product-primitivity argument is standard and completable (needs existence of a=1 mod d1 with xi(a)!=1, glossed but true). Lemma 4 Moebius reduction |T|<=kappa B*(q) with kappa=2^{omega(m)-omega(f)} is correct: pointwise identity (chi psi)(n)=chi*(n)1_{(n,pm)=1} holds, Moebius step and killing of (d,q)>1 terms valid, inner dk-interval bounded by primitive Frolenkov B*. kappa bookkeeping exact; m=2 principal example correctly shows naive kappa=1 version is false, so correction is necessary and sharp for the method. Lemma 5 Q>H/m(1-1/p)-2 correct (K>=floor(H/m)>H/m-1; Q0<H/(pm)+1 via single residue mod pm; spacing argument gives (k-1)pm<H). H0=m(2E+2)/(1-1/p) algebra correct; H>=pm covering argument correct (K>=p consecutive progression terms cover F_p since (m,p)=1, plus at most one zero, giving both signs for p>=3); H=H0 already suffices, H>H0 safe. Frolenkov constants recomputed: C0=74.97367331, c1_even=0.20264236, c2_even=2.38889116, c1_odd=0.15915494, c2_odd=1.73248749 match draft; B*(3)=35.24483 matches h0_table; ratio B*(3)/(sqrt3 log3)=18.5221<19 confirmed; ratio decreasing argument valid given psi1 decreasing (x/(e^{bx}-1) decreasing, verified). Even-majorizes-odd for q>=3 is TRUE with huge margin (diff 16.25 at q=3, 22.8 at 100, 80.4 at 5000) but draft proof omits justification that psi1-psi2>=-0.0076 (needs term1>=term2, i.e. (4/pi)(e^{b2 x}-1)>=e^{b1 x}-1 for x>=sqrt3, which holds: 0.322>=0.273 at sqrt3 and LHS increasing thereafter; draft only notes each psi decreasing). This is a presentation gap with margin >> fp error, not a falsity. originality.rationale: No prior states the exact kappa-corrected finite-p inequality (2)-(4) verbatim -- confirmed against 5 nearest sources: Frolenkov arXiv:1107.0381 is only the PV input B(q) with no intervalxprogression count and no H0; McGown arXiv:1011.4490 is interval-only maximal-run Burgess ~p^{1/4}log p with no uniformity over a mod m; Trevino arXiv:1412.3062 is single short sums for least kth-power nonresidue, no AP restriction, no Q/2 main term; Wright arXiv:1111.2236 is sharp asymptotics as p->infty for AP-pattern counts across 1..p-1, inexplicit, no finite-p error for single short interval intersected with a class; Bordignon-Francis arXiv:2007.08119 stays single-interval. However substantively the delta is mechanical: non-explicit form sum_{n in I, n=a(m)} chi(n) <<_m sqrt(p)log p via Dirichlet orthogonality + PV + Moebius imprimitive reduction is folklore/textbook exercise (ingredients all in Iwaniec-Kowalski Ch.12 PV + imprimitive background + standard orthogonality, as draft itself cites and admits: 'Asymptotic originality is nil -- textbook orthogonality + bookkeeping'). Explicitation by substituting frozen Frolenkov constants, exact N_f census and kappa=2^{omega(m)-omega(f)} adds no new method; kappa/Moebius step is also textbook. A failed verbatim search therefore does not establish priority per audit rule; the substantive combination was routine for an expert. Hence no substantive prior-art gap despite verbatim novelty.

value.rationale: Even if correct and verbatim-new, result is not independently worth finding later. It is a textbook restatement + parameter substitution (p -> pm) + explicitation: orthogonality expansion, conductor q|pm, Moebius kappa factor, elementary Q lower bound and H0 algebra contain no new idea, phenomenon, or technique. H0 corollary is weak: for small p H0>=pm is trivial full-period regime (e.g. H0(101,6)=1275.7 vs pm=606; all p=3,5,7,11 rows trivial); for larger p H0 still requires H>>p for m>1 (e.g. H0(4999,10)=13620 vs pm=49990, factor 3.7 over trivial; H0(4999,18)=30138) or reduces to already-known explicit PV for m=1 (H0(4999,1)=304). No Burgess improvement; PV-based H0 far from p^{1/4} regime. Tables/verification (worst ratio 0.465 at m=1 falling to 0.10-0.24 for m>1, loose by factors 2-10) merely illustrate a proved inequality and confirm the corollary that was already proved -- no discovery, no unexpected behaviour, no downstream lemma demand demonstrated (claimed uses in least-nonresidue-in-progression/search/equidistribution are aspirational, no concrete application with improved range). This matches SCOPE rejection categories: textbook restatement, mere explicitation/parameter substitution, and brute-force-table-without-new-insight, explicitly to be rejected even if correct and new. Draft's own limitations concede looseness for small p, no Burgess gain, and nil asymptotic originality.
